mainEntity.name: I run a hotel, not a short-term let: does this concern me?

acceptedAnswer.text: The CIN applies to hotels as well, so yes for that part. Regulation (EU) 2024/1028 is designed for short-term rentals intermediated by platforms: it concerns you to the extent that you sell through those channels.

mainEntity.name: If I only let through one platform, is there less to do?

acceptedAnswer.text: The obligations are the same, but you have one point of exposure fewer and one concentration risk more: if that listing is suspended over an inconsistent piece of data, the business stops altogether.

mainEntity.name: The platform transmits the data: do I still have to report my guests?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. They are two distinct flows, with different legal bases and different recipients. Reporting guests to the Italian police through the Alloggiati Web portal remains an obligation that falls on you.

mainEntity.name: Should I remove the CIN from my listings for privacy reasons?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, quite the opposite: publishing it in the listings is part of the obligation. It identifies the property, it is not personal data to be protected.

mainEntity.name: Does anything change if I manage properties on behalf of others?

acceptedAnswer.text: The amount of work changes, not the substance: every unit has its own code and its own data, and consistency has to be checked for each. This is the case where channel automation stops being convenient and becomes necessary.
